title: Investigate dynamic kernel recompile thrash causing p95 latency spikes for mixed-quant workloads
creator: Maya Chen
description: During a capacity surge on 2026-03-09 we observed repeated p95 latency spikes for customers using mixed-precision/quantized model variants. The spikes correlated with short bursts of kernel JIT/variant recompilation and kernel cache churn. This ticket tracks investigation findings and post-incident action items to prevent future thrash when the scheduler probes or routes mixed-quant traffic.
steps_reproduced: Run a mixed workload with alternating requests: float16/FP32 model variants and int8 quantized variants with varying sequence lengths (16, 256, 1024).
Simulate scheduler probe window by sending small bursts from new connections that exercise different kernel code paths (attention fused vs unfused, tiled vs untiled).
Measure p95/p99 latency and check GPU-side logs for kernel compile events and CPU-side mutex contention metrics.
Verify kernel cache entries shrink/grow rapidly under load and observe allocator churn on the device-side.
Confirm that disabling the runtime's dynamic kernel recompiler or increasing kernel cache capacity eliminates the spikes in the synthetic test.
timeline: 2026-03-09 14:03 UTC - First customer alert: intermittent p95 spikes reported on hosted endpoints; 2026-03-09 14:12 UTC - On-call triage: increased p95 coincident with capacity surge and schedule-policy probe windows; 2026-03-09 15:00 UTC - Added temporary routing to fallback model variant which reduced median but p95 persisted; 2026-03-09 17:30 UTC - Nightly investigation: kernel compile logs show repeated recompiles of the same kernel family tied to small differences in per-request metadata; 2026-03-10 onwards - Deep dive into kernel cache eviction heuristics and scheduler probe behavior started.
investigation_summary: Correlated telemetry from the runtime, GPU driver logs, and scheduler traces shows frequent kernel variant recompile events during mixed-quant request bursts. The root contributing factors: (1) per-request flags (quantization marker, attention split config) were treated as part of the kernel cache key, resulting in a high cardinality of keys; (2) scheduler's probing behavior intentionally exercises different microconfigurations to detect better kernels and inadvertently triggered recompiles; (3) kernel cache has a limited capacity and eviction policy that prefers LRU which evicted still-warm variants, causing recompile thrash when traffic rotated through variants; (4) a global mutex around the JIT/compile path caused short blocking of worker threads, amplifying p95 under bursty traffic.
root_cause: High-cardinality kernel cache keys combined with aggressive probe-driven kernel selection and a small kernel cache size produced repeated JIT/compile activity and mutex contention. This was exposed by mixed-precision (float/quant) traffic patterns and variable sequence lengths common in customer workloads.
mitigation: Short-term mitigation: increase kernel cache capacity on the affected fleet, add a throttling gate on kernel recompiles, and disable scheduler probe windows for canary clusters serving mixed-quant traffic. Medium-term: decouple transient per-request flags from kernel cache key where safe, add per-variant warm-up grace window, and replace the global compile mutex with a per-key lightweight lock to reduce blocking. Long-term: add automated load tests that exercise mixed-quant rotations to catch regressions in CI and add metrics/alerts for compile rate and cache churn.
action_items: (Owner: Arjun Patel) Immediate: bump kernel cache size from 64 -> 512 entries on runtime-2.4 canaries and verify p95 improvement (ETA: 2026-03-13).
(Owner: Priya Rao) Short-term: add a compile-rate throttle (token-bucket) in the JIT path to limit concurrent recompiles per-GPU and surface metric 'kernel_recompile_throttle_hits' (ETA: 2026-03-20).
(Owner: David López) Short-term: change scheduler probe window config to avoid probing quant-variant models on high-utilization nodes; roll canary (ETA: 2026-03-16).
(Owner: Lina Park) Medium-term: audit kernel cache key components and remove non-essential per-request flags (quantization metadata) after validating correctness locally (ETA: 2026-04-02).
(Owner: Arjun Patel & Infra) Medium-term: change global JIT mutex to sharded per-key locks to reduce cross-request blocking. Add unit tests for lock correctness (ETA: 2026-04-09).

(Owner: SRE - Noah Kim) Monitoring: add dashboards and alerts: compile-rate, kernel-cache-hit-rate, kernel-cache-evictions, recompile-duration, and mutex-wait-time. Create a runbook for compile-thrash (ETA: 2026-03-18).

(Owner: QA - Emma Sullivan) Long-term: add a stable mixed-quant rotation scenario in perf CI that simulates sequence-length variance and ensures p95 stays within threshold across kernel-cache manipulations (ETA: 2026-05-01).
(Owner: PM - Julio Martinez) Communication: prepare a short post-incident summary for impacted customers and update status page template with compile-thrash section (ETA: 2026-03-17).
acceptance_criteria: Kernel recompile rate under mixed-quant synthetic workload is reduced by >= 90% compared to baseline during controlled bursts.
p95 latency for affected endpoints returns to pre-incident baselines under the same mixed-quant rotation tests.
New metrics for kernel_cache_evictions and kernel_recompile_rate are available on Console, with alerts firing when thresholds exceeded.
Scheduler probe config change rolled out to canaries with no regression on median latency or throughput; rollout plan documented.
One integration test in perf CI covers mixed-quant rotations and fails the build if p95 regresses beyond allowed threshold.
follow_up_notes: We observed a small risk that removing quantization flags from the cache key could select a suboptimal kernel for rare edge sequences; will gate removal behind a fallback verification run on canaries.

SRE notes: the initial bump to cache size reduced evictions but increased memory pressure on older GPU models; we constrained the bump to newer fleets only and will evaluate memory telemetry before wider rollout.
PM note: coordinate customer communications for Dedicated customers who saw increased token billing due to retries during the spike window.
Engineering: prioritize medium-term lock sharding work after compile-throttle is validated in staging to maximize risk reduction before the release window.
Add a retrospective session in the next alpha-planning meeting to review scheduling heuristics that probe kernel variants and to determine safer probe policies.
